title: The ampere is fixed by setting the elementary charge to 1.602176634×10^−19 C
summary: NIST defines the ampere by fixing the elementary charge. The same exact number is the 2022 CODATA elementary charge.
body: NIST's electric-current page says the ampere is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the elementary charge e to be 1.602176634 × 10^{−19} when expressed in the unit coulomb, which the page equates to A s, where the second is defined from the caesium frequency. The BIPM defining-constants table prints e as 1.602 176 634 × 10^{−19} C. The 2022 CODATA listing marks e exact. The same NIST page states that the volt is the unit of electric potential difference with 1 V = 1 W/A, and that the ohm is the unit of electric resistance with 1 Ω = 1 V/A.
